analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. It edits two places: the decode-company plain chunk size changes from 512 to 2,048 (head line 324), and a new paragraph near head lines 534-540 describes the effect on durable SSD checkpoint boundaries. It cites `usesWidePrefillChunk` in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. No code, crypto, key handling, authorization, or storage-format changes appear in the supplied evidence.

Security relevance to T-041 (the prefix-cache threat). The new text says that under decode company, a dense Qwen donor with 2,048-token plain chunks leaves no durable boundary in a prompt shorter than 2,048 tokens. It also says the deepest boundary at or below a hint can sit up to 2,047 tokens below it. If the underlying code really behaves this way, fewer and coarser checkpoints are written. That slightly narrows the at-rest footprint and the same-account TTFT oracle for short prompts. It does not weaken any T-041 mitigation. HMAC lookup tags, account-scoped cacheSalt, AES-GCM, the 30-minute TTL, the disk budget, and the KEK-wipe purge are not touched by the documented change.

Unverified: the actual wide-chunk implementation (`usesWidePrefillChunk`) is not supplied. I cannot confirm that the code matches the doc, or that chunk-size changes preserve the parity guarantee cited in the 2026-09-27 measurement report. That is a documentation-accuracy and code-review question for whichever pass sees the Swift change, not a finding here.

No new attack surface, no invalidated threat-model assumptions, and no need for a threat-model update from this docs-only diff.
